predecessors.name: Despotate of Epirus
predecessors.text: 'Thessalonica and its environs' and 'the dynasty's lands in Thessaly' left to Manuel Komnenos Doukas after Theodore's defeat at Klokotnitsa (1230)

successors.name: Empire of Nicaea
successors.text: 'Thessalonica was incorporated into the Nicaean state' under the governor Andronikos Palaiologos (1246)

ledger.x: 1230: after Klokotnitsa Manuel Komnenos Doukas rules the Thessalonican remnant under Bulgarian leave.
1237: Theodore returns to power through his son John.
1239: Manuel Komnenos Doukas takes Larissa and Pharsalos.
1242: John Komnenos Doukas gives up the imperial title and accepts Nicaean authority.

wars.name: Battle of Klokotnitsa
wars.outcome: Theodore's army was destroyed and he was captured; Bulgaria took most of Theodore's Thracian lands and most of Macedonia and Albania; Manuel Komnenos Doukas became Asen's vassal at Thessalonica (1230-37).

wars.name: Manuel Komnenos Doukas's recovery of Thessaly
wars.outcome: Manuel, with Nicaean support, takes Larissa and Pharsalos from John in 1239 and rules Thessaly to about 1241; Michael II of Epirus then occupies it.

wars.name: Nicaean takeover of Thessalonica
wars.outcome: Thessalonica is incorporated into the Nicaean state in 1246; Demetrios is exiled to Asia Minor.

certainty.note: Thirteenth-century frontiers around Thessalonica are known from towns and fortresses, never boundaries; no page delimits the realm.
